answer.title: The network where you own your identity
answer.text: On SimpleX nobody can contact you, or pretend to be somebody you know, unless you give them a link. You join without a phone number or an account. What would you like to do?

image.alt: Glass arcs join points on the surface of the Earth

options.label: Pay and get paid with crypto
Invest before December 10 to reserve your public name

answer.title: A private place for your family
answer.text: On SimpleX nobody can reach your family, or pretend to be one of you, unless one of you gives them a link. Everyone joins without a phone number, on iPhone or Android, and private messaging is free. Where would you like to start?

image.alt: A group of people joined in one private chat

options.label: Keep our chats if a phone is lost

answer.title: Bring everyone at once
answer.text: Today you create a group, name it Family and send its link through any app you already use. Each person installs SimpleX, opens the link and joins while your phone is online. You can let each person in yourself, and you can delete the link when everyone has joined.

options.label: See what we can do together
Run a school or parents' group

answer.title: Get my parents on it
answer.text: Your parents need one link from you, and then they can write to you and call you. Nobody else can reach them unless a link is shared with that person, so their chat list holds only the people they know. The app works in more than 25 languages, and the text can be made larger.

options.label: Make it easy for them to use
Apps don't connect where they live

answer.title: Make it easy for them to use
answer.text: You can make the text larger, give each person a name your parents recognise and put the family in a list of its own. You can do all of this for them when you install the app on their phone.

answer.title: Keep strangers and scammers away
answer.text: SimpleX uses no phone numbers and holds no directory of people, so a stranger has nothing to look up. Someone can reach you only through a link you gave them or a group you are both in, and a request through your address waits until you accept it.

answer.title: Set up my child's phone
answer.text: A child needs no phone number on SimpleX, so an old phone on home Wi-Fi is enough, and nobody can look your child up. Your child can still share a link with anyone. The conditions of use set the minimum age at 13, and your country may set it higher.

answer.title: Move our WhatsApp group
answer.text: A family can move at its own pace. You post the link to your new Family group in your WhatsApp group, and people join when they are ready while the old group keeps working. Old messages stay in WhatsApp for now.

answer.title: Call and share photos
answer.text: You can write, send voice messages of up to five minutes, send photos, videos and files of up to 1 GB, and call each other by audio or video. Groups have replies, mentions and reactions, and you choose how each chat notifies you.

options.label: See what it can and cannot do

answer.title: Call them
answer.text: You can call any contact by audio or video, and the call is end-to-end encrypted. A call connects two people, and by default it goes through a relay server, so the other person does not see your IP address.

answer.title: Share and keep photos
answer.text: You can send up to ten photos at a time. They are reduced in size so that they arrive quickly, and you can send a photo as a file to keep its full quality. Files wait on the servers for 48 hours, or for 7 or 21 days with a supporter or legend badge.

options.label: Keep files longer with a badge
Keep our chats if a phone is lost

answer.title: An audience that stays yours
answer.text: Find what you want to read, or build an audience that stays yours. You hold the keys to your channel, so no platform can take it from you, and your readers stay private. What would you like to do?

image.alt: A channel sending posts to its readers

options.label: Add it to my Substack or YouTube
Run a community by my rules
Get a name for my channel

answer.title: Find channels and groups
answer.text: SimpleX Directory lists more than 500 reviewed groups and channels, and each one opens from a link. A channel shows its recent posts before you join, and other subscribers cannot see that you read it.

answer.title: See how readers stay private
answer.text: A reader opens your link, sees your recent posts and taps Join. New posts then arrive like messages, and the reader can react to them. Other subscribers cannot see who is reading, and the servers cannot connect one channel a person reads to another.

answer.title: Start a channel today
answer.text: Open the app, choose Create public channel, add a name and a picture, and share the link. Chat relays forward your posts from the first day, and you can add contributors who post with you.

options.label: Choose a group or a channel
Put my channel on my website
Find out who can shut me down

answer.title: Choose a group or a channel
answer.text: In a channel you and your contributors post, and readers follow and react. Relays forward each post, so a channel can grow to any size, and its posts are public. In a group every member can write and messages are end-to-end encrypted, and because members connect to each other it strains as it grows.

options.label: Run a community by my rules

answer.title: Move my Telegram channel
answer.text: Keep your Telegram channel and open a SimpleX channel beside it. You share the link with your readers, and those who join remain with you if Telegram blocks the channel. Today you post to both by hand.

options.label: Talk to the team about moving

answer.title: Add it to my Substack or YouTube
answer.text: Your platform keeps working as it does now, and a SimpleX channel gives you a second line to the same people. You add the link to your posts and videos, and readers who join get every new post as a message, whatever an algorithm or a ban does to the other platform.

options.label: Put my channel on my website

answer.title: Put my channel on my website
answer.text: Your channel can appear on your own website. The app gives you a short piece of code, you paste it into your page, and visitors see your recent posts and a Join button before they install anything.

answer.title: Get my channel listed
answer.text: People find you through your link, your name, your web page and SimpleX Directory. You submit your group or channel by sharing its link with the directory bot, and it is usually approved within 24 hours. The directory lists spaces that follow its rules, and anybody can run a directory with other rules.

options.label: Read how to submit my group or channel

answer.title: Work with my team
answer.text: You can give people roles in your channel. Contributors post with you, moderators delete posts and block subscribers, and you can sign every message so that readers can verify it.

options.label: Keep my channel if I lose my phone

answer.title: Run a school or parents' group
answer.text: You set the rules of your group, from who joins and who posts to what remains. Members can talk to admins privately and report problems, and the largest listed group has more than 9,000 members.

options.label: Add a bot to my group

answer.title: Keep spam and abuse out
answer.text: You can delete any message, block a member for everyone, remove people with their messages, review each newcomer and make trusted members moderators. Members report problems to your moderators privately, and groups listed in SimpleX Directory can add a captcha and word filters.

answer.title: Stop an attack now
answer.text: Turn on member review, so that newcomers wait for you. Set new members on your link to observer, so that they can read and cannot post. Block the members who are flooding, and remove them with their messages.

options.label: Read how to protect a group

answer.title: Grow past thousands of members
answer.text: Channels are built for any number of subscribers, because relays forward each post and subscribers never connect to each other. The largest listed channel has 750 subscribers today. Groups run peer-to-peer, and the largest listed group has more than 9,000 members.

options.label: See what a big channel pays

answer.title: Earn from my readers
answer.text: SimpleX shows your readers no ads, and you keep what they pay you. Today you can post your own payment link in your channel.

options.label: Pay and get paid in crypto
Sell to my readers as a business

answer.title: Find out who can shut me down
answer.text: Your channel's keys are on your devices, so no operator can take it from you. Chat relays forward your posts. If a relay stops forwarding them, you add another relay or run your own, and your link, your name and your subscribers remain the same.

options.label: Get a name that stays mine

answer.title: Compare it with Telegram
answer.text: You keep your audience, your rules and your readers' privacy. Telegram and Discord are ahead today on scheduling, pins, statistics, comments, voice rooms and paid subscriptions.

options.label: Tell the team what I need

answer.title: See how abuse is handled
answer.text: Private chats stay private, from us too. Most child abuse material online is shared in places anyone can open, so anyone can report it and we can reach it as anyone can. We check each complaint, then block the link and its files on our servers, without scanning chats and without identifying anyone.

options.label: See what can and can't be removed

answer.title: Report something harmful
answer.text: In a group, press and hold a message and choose Report, and only moderators see it. For illegal content in a public group, send its link to the SimpleX team in the app or to chat@simplex.chat. We check it and answer.

options.label: See what can and can't be removed

answer.title: Appeal a decision
answer.text: We can block a public link or a file on the servers we run, and remove a group from our directory. We can't read private messages, see who talks to whom or reach servers run by others. If you think we got it wrong, write to the team with the link, and a person reads it.

answer.title: One link, a private chat with each customer
answer.text: Give your customers one link, and each of them gets a private chat with you. You answer from your phone or your team's server, and a bot can answer first. The line runs on your own keys and you pay nothing per message, so no platform sits between you and your customers.

image.alt: A public address that customers open to start a private chat

options.label: Get a name customers can find

answer.title: Start today
answer.text: You can start now. Make a profile for your business in the app, turn on Business address and write a welcome message. Share the link or the QR code, and each customer gets a separate chat with you. For now your customers need the SimpleX app.

options.label: Try it with the SimpleX team

answer.title: Bring my customers over
answer.text: You can keep WhatsApp or Telegram while customers move at their own pace. Put your link in your profile, your messages and your receipts. Each customer who opens it gets a private chat with you, and you pay nothing per message there.

answer.title: Send updates to my customers
answer.text: A customer who connected to you stays connected, so you can write to them later in the same chat. A bot can do this today, one chat at a time, and it can send what your own systems produce, such as an order update.

options.label: Build it with the bot library

answer.text: Your customer sees your name, logo and welcome before sending anything, and the first message goes with the request to connect. They choose the name you see.

options.label: Reach a customer who has left
Try it with the SimpleX team

answer.text: Messages are end-to-end encrypted between your customer and you, and servers hold no profiles or contact lists. You read what your customer writes and you keep it, so it is yours to protect. If you use an AI provider, it reads what the bot sends it.

answer.title: Let AI answer first
answer.text: A bot can answer first and bring in a person when the customer asks. SimpleX's own line works this way. The customer chooses the AI, the AI answers from a file the team wrote, and the first reply from the team ends it. You run the bot yourself, so you pay your AI provider and nobody else for each answer.

options.label: Read how the support bot works

answer.title: Answer as a team
answer.text: On your own, you answer in the app. With a team, your line runs on your own server, each new chat appears as a card in your team's group, and anyone on the team can join it with one tap. The customer sees who is answering. Today a developer sets this up.

options.label: Run the bot on my server
Read what happens if I lose the server

answer.title: Work with my team here
answer.text: Your team can talk in a private group today, with files of up to 1 GB, voice messages and calls between two people.

options.label: Bring the whole team at once

answer.title: Stop depending on a platform
answer.text: On other channels a platform holds your number or account, sets the price of each message and can restrict you. On SimpleX your line is a set of keys on your device, and your address sits on servers you choose, your own among them. If you move your address, the customers you already talk to stay connected.

options.label: Read what happens if I lose my phone

answer.title: Pay and get paid in a private chat
answer.text: You can reach a seller, a friend or a service on SimpleX without a phone number or an account, and pay them from the wallet you already use. The address they give you stays inside the end-to-end encrypted conversation.

options.label: Get paid for what I sell
Buy a name or a badge with crypto
Check whether SimpleX has a coin

answer.title: Pay someone in a chat
answer.text: Today you ask for an address in the chat, copy it and pay from your wallet. The address stays inside the end-to-end encrypted conversation, so servers cannot read it.

options.label: Keep this payment apart from others

answer.title: Get paid for what I sell
answer.text: Independent sellers and exchange services already publish a SimpleX address, because a customer can write to them without an account. A business address gives each customer a separate chat with you, and a bot can answer first. Until requests arrive, the payment itself happens in the customer's wallet.

answer.title: Keep payments apart from chats
answer.text: The network has no user identifiers, so no account ties your payments to your chats. A public chain still records what each address did, so use a new address for each payment, which Monero does for you. The store keeps the record of what you buy for tax, and it cannot see your chats. A name's record is public.

answer.title: Buy a name or a badge with crypto
answer.text: You can buy a supporter badge with Bitcoin, Monero or a card and redeem the code in the app, with no account. SimpleX names will go on sale at simplex.domains, and you can pay for them with Monero or Bitcoin.

answer.title: Check whether SimpleX has a coin
answer.text: SimpleX has no coin of its own, and you pay for names and badges with coins that already exist. Community Credits are the way communities will pay for servers. They are not a tradable token, there will be no pre-sale or emission, and they can be redeemed only with listed network operators.

options.label: See why names use a blockchain

answer.title: Build what people reach in a chat
answer.text: Build something people reach in a chat. A bot on SimpleX needs no account, token or review, and it runs on your laptop with no open port. It holds its own keys, so no platform can suspend it.

image.alt: A bot answering in a chat

options.label: Move a bot I already run
Put chat in my own app or site
Get paid for what I build
Run a server or a relay

answer.title: Add a bot to my group
answer.text: Install a package, write ten lines and open the address your bot prints. Anyone with that address can talk to it, with no sign-up on either side. If your bot goes offline, messages wait on the server for up to 21 days.

options.label: Can I build a product on this?

answer.title: Use another language
answer.text: Any language works today. Run the terminal client as a local server, and your program exchanges JSON with it over a WebSocket. Node.js and Python have libraries, Rust has a community library, and the commands and events are documented.

answer.title: Give it buttons and menus
answer.text: A bot has a command menu today, commands a person taps in a message, messages it can update, streamed text and Markdown. The calculator bot shows how far this goes, with a working keypad in one message.

answer.title: Move my bot too
answer.text: Your bot keeps its logic. You change the calls that send and receive, your users connect through a new address, and your bot then needs no company's token. In January 2026 WhatsApp barred general-purpose AI chatbots from its Business API in most countries.

options.label: I also run a Telegram channel

answer.title: Send alerts to my phone
answer.text: Get a message on your phone from a script, a server or a sensor, with no phone number. The terminal client sends one from a single command today, and six independent projects use SimpleX this way.

options.label: Make a bot that answers back

answer.title: Help people find it
answer.text: People reach your bot through its link, a QR code or your website, and a public name gives it an address they can remember and check. Your site can publish that address for people and software to find.

options.label: Get paid for what I build
Publish my address on my site

answer.title: Get paid for what I build
answer.text: You keep your customers and choose how to charge. A bot can send a payment link or an invoice as a message today, and nothing stands between you and the buyer. The app has no payment step yet.

answer.title: Run it on a server
answer.text: A bot is a program with its own database. Run it on a laptop or a small server. It makes outgoing connections only, so it needs no domain or certificate, and for volume you can use PostgreSQL on Linux.

answer.title: See what my bot learns
answer.text: Your bot sees the messages sent to it and the profile a person chose to share, which can be random. You hold no phone numbers or emails, so you have none to lose. In a group, a bot reads the group.

answer.title: Put chat in my own app or site
answer.text: Put SimpleX in your own product. The Node.js and Python libraries include the whole core, so a server, a desktop app, a wallet or a payment service can use them today to message its users.

options.label: Can I build a product on this?

answer.title: Can I build a product on this?
answer.text: The network is open, and nobody has to approve what you build. The software is AGPL-3.0. The protocol is licensed to a non-profit foundation permanently, so it stays available whoever owns the company.

answer.title: Run my own servers
answer.text: Anyone can run SimpleX servers, and about 1,000 are run by volunteers at their own cost. You can run a messaging server, a file server or a chat relay for channels. We plan that big channels pay for delivery, and that operators earn up to 65% of what they pay.

options.label: Ask how the share will work

answer.title: Connect my AI
answer.text: An AI on SimpleX is a contact in your chats. It sees what you send it and nothing else in the app, and SimpleX asks you for no phone number or email. What do you want it to do for you?

options.label: Control my agent from my phone
See who reads what I ask
Let it use bots and services
Add a bot to my group

answer.title: Control my agent from my phone
answer.text: Connect Claude Code on your computer to the SimpleX app by scanning a code. You write prompts in a chat on your phone, and it asks there before it connects, sends or leaves. You need no bot token, and no port open to the internet.

options.label: Let it use bots and services

answer.title: Approve what it does
answer.text: Your agent posts a card in a private chat that says what it wants to do and to whom. One tap approves or rejects it. You can approve all its messages to one chat, and take that back at any time.

answer.title: Let it use bots and services
answer.text: Your agent can connect to any bot and use the commands it offers, and one bot can serve people and software. We have drafted how services declare their tools, so SimpleX may become a network where agents find and call services with nobody in the middle.

answer.title: See who reads what I ask
answer.text: It depends on where the AI runs. On your phone or your own machine, nobody else reads anything. With Claude Code, Anthropic reads what the session sends it, as it does without SimpleX. The operator of a hosted assistant reads each request and cannot tell who you are unless you say so. SimpleX servers deliver encrypted messages and read none of this.

answer.title: Safety for your private life
answer.text: Your chats hold your family life, your health, your money and your work, and on SimpleX they stay between you and the people you choose. Nobody can reach you without a link from you, and no company holds a list of the people you talk to. What would you like to protect first?

image.alt: What a server can and cannot see of a message

options.label: Keep my money and accounts safe
Keep my data out of leaks, ads and AI
Protect my chats if I lose my phone
See how it is safer than WhatsApp
Why does this matter to me?

answer.title: Why does this matter to me?
answer.text: Everyone locks the front door and keeps a bank PIN private, and nobody finds that strange. The people you talk to say just as much about you, because they include your doctor, your bank, your lawyer and your children's school. Companies use such lists to set your prices, and the lists get stolen, as AT&T reported in 2024 about the call and text records of nearly all its customers. SimpleX keeps no such list, so nobody can sell it or steal it.

options.label: Keep my data out of leaks, ads and AI
See how it is safer than WhatsApp
See who can see my messages

answer.title: Keep my data out of leaks, ads and AI
answer.text: Your messages, your contacts and your profile are stored on your phone. Servers pass on encrypted messages and delete them once they are delivered, so a leak from a server would show no chat history and no address book. We can't read your chats, so we can't target you with ads or train an AI on them, and we have no user data to sell.

options.label: See who can see my messages
See how it is safer than WhatsApp
Find out how it is paid for

answer.title: See what servers can see
answer.text: Only the people in a conversation can read it. Messages are end-to-end encrypted and padded to one size, so a server can neither read them nor measure them. A server sees the random addresses of the queues it hosts and the times of messages. With private routing, on by default, the server your contact chose does not see your IP address. Your internet provider sees which servers you connect to.

options.label: Keep today's messages safe in future

answer.title: Learn how the privacy works
answer.text: Most apps give you one number or username for all your conversations, so all of them are tied to you. SimpleX gives each conversation its own random addresses, one for each direction and usually on different servers, and your contacts and groups are stored only on your device. To connect, people share a link or a QR code that also holds the encryption keys, so servers cannot replace them.

options.label: Read why who you talk to matters
Read the hard choices we made

answer.title: See what SimpleX cannot protect
answer.text: A contact can keep what you send, and malware on your phone can read what the app shows. Someone who can watch the traffic of both people can confirm that they communicate. The servers that deliver your messages see your IP address unless you use a VPN or Tor.

options.label: Compare it with WhatsApp or Signal

answer.title: Check it is really them
answer.text: Anyone can copy a name and a picture, so a profile can't tell you who is writing. The keys are part of the link you share, so servers cannot replace them. To check that nobody replaced the link on the way, compare your security code in person or in a call, and the app then marks the contact as verified.

answer.title: Keep today's messages safe in future
answer.text: A future quantum computer could read messages recorded today, so direct chats are protected against that by default. Groups use the same encryption without that extra step for now.

answer.title: Keep my group private
answer.text: A group's members and profile are stored on members' devices, and each message is end-to-end encrypted for each member. Members are introduced through the person who invited them, so to be sure of a connection you compare security codes. Public channels work differently, because posts are public and relays protect who reads them.

options.label: Check who I am talking to
Bring my family into a group

answer.title: Apps don't connect where they live
answer.text: Some countries and networks stop messaging apps from connecting, and this can separate families and friends across borders. The app still connects through a VPN, a SOCKS proxy or Tor, and your messages stay end-to-end encrypted on the way. It does not depend on the simplex.chat website, so it keeps working when the site can't be reached.

answer.title: Connect now
answer.text: If a friend or an organisation gives you a proxy, open Network & servers, turn on the SOCKS proxy and enter the address. For a proxy that is not Tor, turn off random credentials. With Tor, start Orbot first. If someone runs a server your network can reach, you can add it and change the receiving address of each conversation.

options.label: Use a server of my own
See the settings step by step

answer.title: Help someone connect
answer.text: If you are somewhere SimpleX works, you can help a person who cannot connect by running a small server on port 443 and giving them its address. The server sees their IP address and the times of their traffic, and it cannot read their messages. Give the address only to people you know.

answer.title: Protect my IP address
answer.text: Your IP address shows roughly where you are, and your bank, your payment apps and your crypto exchange record it each time you log in. If a messenger or a contact also sees it, a leak can connect your chats to your accounts and your home. By default SimpleX sends messages through a forwarding server and calls through a relay, so the people you talk to and their servers never see your IP address, and preset servers keep no log of it.

options.label: Keep my payments apart from my chats
See who can see my messages

answer.title: Use our own servers
answer.text: Anyone can run servers. SimpleX Chat and Flux are preset, and when both are enabled the app uses servers of both in each conversation, so neither learns who talks to whom. You can turn either off, add others or use your own, and a conversation can move to another server.

answer.title: Protect my chats if I lose my phone
answer.text: Your chats are kept in an encrypted database on your phone, and a passcode on the app keeps them closed to whoever finds it. Messages can disappear when both sides agree, a profile can sit behind its own password, and a second passcode can erase everything. We can't wipe a lost phone for you, because you have no account, so set the lock before you need it.

options.label: See what the app cannot protect

answer.title: Fix notifications and battery
answer.text: On Android the app keeps its own background connection, so Google is not involved, and you can switch to a check every 10 minutes. On iPhone, notifications pass through Apple and the SimpleX Chat push server, and neither sees the content or the sender. On both, you choose how much a notification shows on the lock screen.

options.label: Fix something that does not work
See what a push server learns

answer.title: Check the claims for myself
answer.text: The apps and servers are open source. Trail of Bits reviewed the implementation in 2022 and the cryptographic design in 2024, and a third audit was completed in 2026 and will be published. You can rebuild the servers, the Linux apps and Android from source, though not the iOS app. We publish every request for user data that we receive.

answer.title: See how it is safer than WhatsApp
answer.text: WhatsApp and Signal encrypt your messages, and Telegram does this only in secret chats that you start yourself. All three register you with a phone number, so your safety rests on a company's promise about what that account reveals, and a breach or a change of owner can end a promise. SimpleX registers nobody, so the protection is part of how the network is built. These apps are ahead today on linked devices, backups and group calls.

options.label: See who can see my messages
See what it can and cannot do

answer.title: Talk in confidence at work
answer.text: Some work depends on confidence, such as a doctor with a patient, a lawyer with a client, a union with a member or a journalist with a source. On SimpleX people reach you through a link, without a phone number, an email or an account, and each person has a separate conversation.

answer.title: Report wrongdoing to a journalist
answer.text: If you have seen wrongdoing at work, you can tell a journalist in confidence, without a phone number or an email. Install SimpleX on a device your employer does not manage, use a network they do not run, and scan the QR code on the newsroom's own tip page. Choose a random profile when you connect, and add your first message to the request. Someone who watches the traffic of both you and the newsroom can confirm that you communicate.

options.label: Find a newsroom in the directory
Read how to share with the press

answer.title: Send a document
answer.text: In the app you can send a file of up to 1 GB, end-to-end encrypted, and preset file servers keep it for 48 hours. The apps remove metadata from static images, and the iOS app also from videos. A document sent as a file keeps its metadata, so check it first or send a screenshot.

options.label: Send a file from a browser

answer.title: Let sources reach me
answer.text: You can open a tip line today. Create a separate chat profile, make a SimpleX address and put it on your tip page as a link and a QR code. When you meet someone, show a one-time link as a QR code, which works for one person. You can delete the address at any time and keep the people who already reached you.

options.label: Tell sources how to write safely

answer.title: Reach readers in another country
answer.text: If your site can't be reached where your readers live, a SimpleX channel reaches them without a phone number or an account, and readers do not see each other. A reader with something to tell you writes to your tip address in a separate end-to-end encrypted chat. Where SimpleX itself can't connect, readers use a proxy.

options.label: Open a tip line beside it

answer.title: Protect my clients or patients
answer.text: Lawyers, doctors, advisers, unions and helplines all depend on people speaking freely. You publish one address and each client gets a separate conversation, with no phone number or account on either side. With a business address, colleagues can join a client's conversation.

options.label: Open a line for my clients
Talk to customers as a business

answer.title: Compare it with SecureDrop
answer.text: SecureDrop needs Tor Browser from a source and its own servers at a newsroom, while Signal is familiar and registers each person with a phone number. Hush Line and GlobaLeaks take a first message in a browser. SimpleX needs the app on the source's device, but it uses no phone number or account on either side and it keeps a two-way conversation.

options.label: Add SimpleX beside what I use

answer.title: I am writing about SimpleX
answer.text: Key facts and the timeline give each number with its date and source, and the transparency reports show every request for user data. Ask us anything before you publish.

answer.title: Infrastructure for all communications
answer.text: SimpleX is the only messaging network without user identifiers. It has 600,000+ monthly users, 20x more than at our 2023 round, and 200+ people have invested on Wefunder so far. We plan to earn from businesses and big channels, while private messaging stays free. What would you like to know first?

image.alt: People connected through the network without user identifiers

options.label: What do I get if I invest?

answer.title: How fast is it growing?
answer.text: We estimate that over 600,000 people use SimpleX every month, up 70% in six months and 20x since our 2023 round. Until August 2026 we paid for no marketing. People found it through more than 200 reviews, posts and videos in over 20 languages, and the app has been downloaded over 3 million times.

answer.title: How do you count users?
answer.text: We can't count people, because the network has no user identifiers. So 600,000 is our estimate, made from app store reports and the traffic through our servers. Those servers deliver over 20 million messages a day.

answer.title: Do people stay?
answer.text: About one monthly user in five opens SimpleX every day, up from 17% to 21% in the six months to April, and about one in four in the US and Germany. Public groups in our directory hold over 160,000 memberships. Not everyone stays: a wave that came from Telegram in 2024 fell by about a quarter within a month.

answer.title: Who are they?
answer.text: By our estimate, the largest groups are people who put their safety and privacy first, people in countries that restrict other apps, and families. Creators run thousands of public groups and channels, over 50 businesses support customers here, developers gave the project over 19,000 GitHub stars, and volunteers run about 1,000 servers. Each group makes the network more useful to the others.

options.label: See how a family uses it

answer.title: What is driving it?
answer.text: People bring the people they talk to, and independent reviewers recommend SimpleX. Growth jumps when people lose an app they relied on, through a ban or a change of rules. Groups and channels can bring whole audiences at once, and they can't yet be found from inside the app, so that lever is still ahead of us.

answer.title: What happens next?
answer.text: The name sale is our first real test of revenue. We plan to add search for groups and channels in the app this year, then business chat for websites and paid servers for big channels, and widgets inside chats in 2027. Our goals for the next two years are to launch revenue, reach 1–2 million monthly users and cover our costs.

options.label: How could I make a return?

answer.title: How will it make money?
answer.text: We have no user data to sell, so private messaging stays free and shows no ads. We plan to earn from those who want to be found or need more capacity: businesses and channels buy names, businesses pay for website chat, and big channels pay for servers. Supporter badges are on sale now. We have earned almost nothing so far, and this plan is unproven.

options.label: What do big channels pay for?
Can this earn as much as ads?

answer.title: What do names earn?
answer.text: A public name lets people find a channel or a business without a long link, and only the owner's key controls it. Names will go on sale at about $50 a year. At that price, 10,000 names would cover our operating cost of about $360,000 a year. In 2022 Telegram sold over $50 million of usernames in about four weeks, with far more users than we have.

options.label: Check whether a name is free

answer.title: Who would buy 10,000 names?
answer.text: First the owners of groups and channels: over 500 are listed in our directory, and thousands more exist. Then the businesses that already talk to customers here, brands that want to protect their own name, and people who name a bot or an agent. The public sale will show how many of them buy.

answer.title: What do businesses pay for?
answer.text: A business gets a private line to each customer without holding phone numbers or accounts, so it has no contact list to lose. We are building chat for any website, in one line of code, with nothing for a visitor to install. We expect $20–100 a month per business. Over 50 businesses already support customers here, and they would be the first customers.

options.label: Why pay when chat widgets are free?

answer.title: Who are these businesses?
answer.text: Most are crypto services, shops, and hosting and VPN providers, and they came without any sales effort. None pays us yet, because we have nothing to sell them beyond a name. They show that businesses want a line to customers that no platform controls, and whether they will pay for more is what we have to prove.

options.label: Why pay when chat widgets are free?

answer.title: Why pay when chat widgets are free?
answer.text: We won't win on chat features, because good free tools exist. We can win where a conversation depends on confidence, such as ethics lines, HR and legal advice. There, the product is that no provider holds a list of who asked, and a provider with accounts can only promise that.

options.label: What do big channels pay for?

answer.title: What do big channels pay for?
answer.text: A channel can reach any number of readers, because relays forward each post. Big channels that grow past the free tier would pay for delivery, at an expected $20–50 a month. Operators would earn up to 65% of that, several times their cost, and we would keep the rest.

options.label: Can this earn as much as ads?

answer.title: What can users buy?
answer.text: Supporter badges have been on sale since September, from $7 a month, by card, Bitcoin or Monero. A badge sends larger files that stay available longer, and it cannot identify who bought it. Users have also donated over $650,000 for an app they can use for free, including a large gift from Vitalik Buterin.

options.label: What do I get if I invest?

answer.title: Can this earn as much as ads?
answer.text: Ad networks earn from watching people. We think that weakens as AI agents do the looking, because an agent ignores ads and can pay small amounts within a budget its owner sets. A chat network can already earn more from services than from ads: in 2025 Tencent, the owner of WeChat, earned about $32B from payments, financial services and cloud, and about $20B from ads. We plan to earn a share of such payments, with nobody identified. This is our belief, and it is unproven.

answer.title: Why would the company earn?
answer.text: The code is open, so anyone can copy it, and we want others to build on the network. The company keeps what a fork can't take: the app and its store listings, the brand, the preset servers, and a share of what names and payments earn, protected by its veto in the SimpleX Network Consortium. The protocols are licensed to a non-profit foundation, so the network survives whoever owns the company.

answer.title: How big can this get?
answer.text: WhatsApp has over 3 billion monthly users and Telegram over 1 billion, so messaging is among the largest networks there are. We think the next one won't be built on identifiers, because AI makes phone numbers and usernames easy to abuse. SimpleX may become the network people and their AI agents use, and we are at the very start of that.

answer.title: Why now?
answer.text: If an AI can copy your voice and your face and fake your phone number, a phone number proves nothing. On SimpleX nobody can contact you or pretend to be somebody you know unless you gave them a link. AI also makes surveillance of private life and deplatforming cheap, so more people may want a network that keeps no record of who they talk to.

answer.title: What does AI change?
answer.text: Each new kind of computer has needed a new network: mainframes the Internet, PCs the web, phones the app stores. We believe AI models are the next kind of computer, and people already work with them in chat. You will want your agents to answer to you, with an identity no company can switch off. SimpleX may become that network, and our company plans to earn from it without owning it.

answer.title: What is the long-term goal?
answer.text: Telephony, email and the web each converged on one protocol. Messaging has not, because every app builds its own experience. We plan widgets inside chats in 2027, so that anyone can build that experience on one open network. SimpleX might become the network messaging converges on, owned by nobody.

answer.title: Why can't others copy it?
answer.text: Other networks are built on user identifiers, so they would have to rebuild from scratch to remove them, and the big ones earn from those identifiers. Their privacy is a promise that lasts until the company is compromised. Ours is in the architecture: we hold no list of who talks to whom, so there is nothing to hand over. A newcomer would need users, creators, businesses, developers and servers all at once.

options.label: What about Session, Matrix and Nostr?

answer.title: What about Signal and WhatsApp?
answer.text: Signal and WhatsApp now offer usernames, so that other people don't see your number. Anyone who knows or guesses the username can still reach you, and the company still holds the account. That is the weakness of a phone number with a better promise. They see the problem, and their architecture doesn't let them solve it.

answer.title: What about Session, Matrix and Nostr?
answer.text: Session gives each person one permanent key, and Matrix and Nostr identify you by an account or a key, so an identifier still links your conversations. SimpleX gives you none, because every conversation has its own addresses. No other network also combines channels that scale with ownership that no operator can take away.

answer.title: Has anyone checked this?
answer.text: Trail of Bits audited SimpleX in 2022, 2024 and 2026, and the last report will be published soon. The code is open source, the servers and the Android and Linux apps can be rebuilt from it, and independent reviewers such as Privacy Guides recommend SimpleX. We publish every request for user data in our transparency reports.

answer.title: Who is behind it?
answer.text: Evgeny Poberezkin designed SimpleX. He led engineering at MailOnline and Stream, and he created Ajv, a JavaScript library with over 1.5 billion downloads a month. The team is five people, three of them here since the start, and everyone ships code with AI tools. All of this was built on $1.7M of investment.

answer.title: Who has invested?
answer.text: Nick Rogers, former CPTO of Stream, leads this round. He first invested in 2022 and has invested again. Jack Dorsey led our 2023 round, with Asymmetric Capital Partners, and Vitalik Buterin donated to the project. Nearly 200 people have invested in this round, and three of our four advisors are among them.

options.label: What do I get if I invest?

answer.title: What do investors say?
answer.text: Many of our investors use the app. One wrote: "I use SimpleX, I've introduced my family to it, and I genuinely think you've built a better approach to private communication." Another: "Investing in SimpleX Chat aligns with my values as a parent who prioritizes digital privacy." 65 of them say why on Wefunder.

options.label: What do I get if I invest?

answer.title: Hear from the founder
answer.text: On November 19 at 18:00 UTC, Evgeny Poberezkin and Bruce McCarthy talk live about why AI is breaking trust, how SimpleX solves it and how it will make money. You can ask your questions there, or on Wefunder at any time.

answer.title: What could go wrong?
answer.text: This is an early company with almost no revenue, and you could lose all the money you invest. Our revenue plan is unproven, growth can slow, and you may not be able to sell for a long time. A private network also draws hard questions about abuse and the law, and we would rather answer them here. Please read the risks on Wefunder too.

options.label: How do you deal with abuse?
How could I make a return?
Can I trust the user number?

answer.title: How do you deal with abuse?
answer.text: Nobody can contact you on SimpleX unless you give them a link, so it is a poor tool for scams and for reaching strangers. That is why families move here. Private chats stay private, also from us. Illegal content in public groups can be reported, and we remove such links and files from the servers we run, without scanning chats or identifying anyone.

answer.title: What about the law?
answer.text: We took legal advice on what server operators are responsible for, and our Form C discloses it. We answer valid requests and publish every one in our transparency reports. Servers hold no profiles or contact lists, so there is little to give: in 2025 we received 12 requests and had no responsive information.

options.label: What if it can't connect somewhere?

answer.title: How could I make a return?
answer.text: You may benefit if the company grows. From today's point of view, the most likely routes to a return are an IPO or a sale to other investors, and that may take many years. Our goals for the next two years are to launch revenue, reach 1–2 million monthly users, cover our costs and raise a next round. You may not be able to sell before then, or for longer.

options.label: What do I get if I invest?

answer.title: What do I get if I invest?
answer.text: Every investor receives a supporter badge, from one month at $100 to a year as a legend at $10,000. From $500 you also receive a public SimpleX name: 8 or more letters from $500, 7 from $1,000 and 6 from $5,000. It is registered for 5 years while early bird terms apply, and for 3 years after that. Invest before December 10 to reserve yours ahead of the public sale.

What can a name do for me?

answer.title: What can a name do for me?
answer.text: A name opens your channel or your address, as #example or @example.simplex, in place of a long link. You can point it at your own address so that people find you by name, or keep it for a channel or a business you start later. You control it with your own key.

answer.title: How do I invest?
answer.text: You invest on Wefunder, a regulated funding portal, from $100. You create an account, confirm your identity, choose an amount and pay by card, bank transfer or wire. Wefunder adds a payment fee, and it shows the fee before you confirm. People outside the US can invest too, if the law of their country allows it.

options.label: What do I reveal by investing?

answer.title: What do I reveal by investing?
answer.text: Investing is the one place where a real name is needed. Wefunder must verify who you are and asks for a tax ID, and we receive investors' details for legal and tax records. None of this touches your SimpleX chats or your contacts, because the network has no user identifiers to link it to.

options.label: See what others can learn about me

answer.title: What are the terms?
answer.text: The terms of this round are on Wefunder: what you receive, the price and the dates. We keep them in that one place, because Wefunder is the regulated home of this round, and please read them before you invest. If anything is unclear, ask on the Wefunder page, and we answer there in public.

answer.title: Can I invest later?
answer.text: We can't promise another round that is open to everyone. That depends on how revenue and users grow. The name perk has its own date: invest before December 10 to reserve your name ahead of the public sale.

answer.title: Help without money
answer.text: Thank you for wanting to help. You can tell people about SimpleX, translate it, run a server or buy a supporter badge. What suits you?

answer.title: Tell people about it
answer.text: Reviews by people in their own language reach further than anything we can publish. We answer your questions before you publish, and we add your review to our list. A QR code works on a wall or a slide, and a public name works in a podcast.

options.label: Make a channel for my group

answer.title: Translate these pages
answer.text: People who use SimpleX translate it in Weblate. Start with the Android app, and we can add you to the translators' group.

answer.title: Check something I heard
answer.text: If you heard something about SimpleX and are not sure it is true, here is what we state, with sources, and what SimpleX cannot do.

options.label: Find out if it is a crypto project

answer.text: SimpleX Chat is free on iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows and Linux, and in a terminal. You need no phone number or email to start. Once it is installed, you connect to someone with a link or a QR code.

image.alt: The SimpleX Chat desktop app with a list of chats

options.label: Find out which version I need
Fix something that does not work

answer.title: Send them an invitation
answer.text: Create a one-time link in the app and send it to one person, or show its QR code when you meet or on a video call. To be reachable by many people, create a SimpleX address, which you can delete at any time and keep your contacts.

answer.title: Find out which version I need
answer.text: The iPhone app needs iOS 15 or newer, and the Android app needs Android 8 or newer. You can install on Android from Google Play, from F-Droid or as an APK, and desktop apps run on Mac, Windows and Linux. You can verify a release and rebuild it yourself.

answer.title: Fix a call that fails
answer.text: When a message is late, a call fails or an error appears, tell us what you see in the Ask SimpleX Team chat, and we help you fix it. The FAQ covers the common causes.

options.label: It does not connect where I am

answer.title: See what it can and cannot do
answer.text: SimpleX has voice messages, calls between two people, disappearing messages, reactions, replies, mentions, groups, channels and file transfer. Group calls, stickers and shared location are not in the app today, and one profile works on one device at a time.

options.label: Tell the team what I need

answer.title: Move something else
answer.text: You do not have to leave all at once. Your old app keeps working while people join you here through a link, and SimpleX has no phone numbers to match, so each person moves by opening that link. What are you moving?

answer.title: Keep our chats if a phone is lost
answer.text: Your chats and contacts are kept on your phone and nowhere else. If you still have the old phone, you can move everything to a new one by scanning a code, and you can export a backup by hand at any time. Without a backup a lost phone takes its chats with it.

options.label: Use it on a tablet or computer

answer.title: Use it on a tablet
answer.text: One profile works on one device at a time. The desktop app can use your phone's profiles while both are on the same network, and it can also hold profiles of its own. In a browser you can send a file and read a channel's web page.

options.label: Send a file from a browser

answer.text: A name lets people find you without a long link. #example opens your channel, and @example.simplex opens your business address. You control it with your own key, so no server can take it away, and if your link stops working you can point the name to a new one.

answer.title: Use a code I was given
answer.text: A code is a prepaid badge or name. You redeem it in the app, and you need no account. Anyone can give you one.

answer.title: See what a big channel pays
answer.text: Private messaging, groups, channels, a business address and the support bot are free. A supporter badge costs $7 a month, and a public name is expected to cost about $50 a year. You pay your AI provider yourself, so our price does not grow with seats or answered chats.

options.label: Find out why messaging stays free

answer.title: Find out what it costs
answer.text: Private messaging stays free, and the app shows no ads. SimpleX Chat plans to earn from public names, business messaging and servers for big channels, and users have donated over $650,000 so far. If you want larger files and longer storage, you can buy a supporter badge.

answer.title: Ask the team
answer.text: A bot answers first, and you can ask for the team at any time. The team replies within 24 hours, or 48 hours at weekends.

answer.title: See who keeps it independent
answer.text: The protocols are licensed permanently to a non-profit foundation, so they stay available whoever owns the company. The foundation and SimpleX Chat are parties to the SimpleX Network Consortium, which other organizations can join, and anyone can run servers.
